## Remarks

Cancellation: an abort before the run starts prevents it. An abort during the run rejects immediately with `OperationCancelledError`<!-- -->, and the transport stops the automation process. Whatever the app had already done by then stays done: whether it completed the operation is unknown after a mid-run abort.

Reference resolution: `resolve` resolves the references the provider can also convert at operation positions (phases/13 D7, native conversion scope), and identity collections of them: a single identity reference to a resource the app finds by its identifier, carrying, exactly when the resource's get records a parent, its container in the same form. The object is found exactly as conversion finds it, by the codec, container first, and read as the resource's get reads its item, in one automation process per request. A missing object fails with `TargetNotFoundError` naming the referenced resource, with `entryIndex` for an identity collection's entry; a missing container names the container's resource. An empty identity collection resolves to `[]` without starting an automation process; the runtime has already run permission, governance, approval and audit for it, as for any resolution. Every other reference (a selector, a container the target is not found within, a missing container, or one to a resource outside that scope) fails with `InternalError` naming the form, before any automation runs.
